contentHtml:
UAE trade license verification is an important step, do not miss it. The step validates legitimacy and compliance with local regulations. Having a valid trade license means a business operates within the legal framework. This fosters trust but also safeguards stakeholders.

Securing them from potential fraud or illegal activities. Engaging with businesses without proper licensing can lead to legal complications. Further financial losses, and reputational damage. This happens frequently in the UAE’s highly regulated business environment.

In this guide, we’ll walk you through the:

  • Various methods are available to verify trade licenses, including
  • Online platforms, steps to check trade license Dubai validity, and
  • Essential tips for ensuring accurate verification.

Why Trade License Verification is Important in the UAE

Obtaining a UAE trade license is a legal requirement. The business can operate legally by having it. A trade license is an official government document. It authorizes a company to carry out commercial activities in the country. Businesses with this document must adhere to strict regulations.

While promoting transparency, and accountability. As a result, it fosters a safe and reliable market for consumers/investors. The trade license verification is a protective measure. Particularly for any individual or organization engaging in business activities. Giving an assurance that all operations are lawful.

When You Should Verify a Trade License:

You should verify a trade license before signing any contract. Verification is also important before making payments or starting a business partnership. It helps you confirm that the company operates legally and holds valid approvals. Verifying process protects you from fraud, expired licenses, and compliance risks. With regular checks, you will build trust and maintain secure business dealings in the UAE.

Before Signing a Contract or Partnership:

Always verify the other party’s trade license before you sign any agreement. This confirms the company legally exists. It can perform the agreed services. The step protects you from entering into contracts with expired or suspended businesses.

Before Making Payments or Investments:

Never release payments or investments without verifying the license first. In the UAE, many fraud cases involve valid-looking documents from unlicensed entities. A quick check helps you avoid costly mistakes.

When Hiring Service Providers or Consultants:

PROs, consultants, and service providers must hold valid licenses for their activities. Verification makes sure they operate legally and reduces the risks of poor service or disputes.

During Due-Diligence & Vendor Onboarding:

In due diligence, trade license verification plays a key role. It aids you in assessing compliance. You’ll get ownership clarity and operational legitimacy before onboarding vendors/suppliers.

When Checking a Competitor or Supplier:

Verifying a competitor or supplier’s license helps you understand their business scope. You can better understand jurisdiction and credibility. It also supports fair competition and informed decision-making.

Types of Trade Licenses in the UAE

The UAE issues three primary trade license types. These are based on the nature of the business:

  1. Commercial License: Issued for companies in trading goods or commodities. This could involve importing/exporting/selling products. This license type applies to businesses in retail. The wholesale business and distribution sectors can also use it to carry out their operations
  2. Professional License: Reserved for individuals or firms providing specialized professional services. Including consultancy, legal, and technical services. Accountants, engineers, and design professionals hold this license.
  3. Industrial License: The industrial license is required for companies in manufacturing or industrial operations. It applies to businesses in converting raw materials into finished products. Also, operating production facilities like factories.
  4. Tourism License: Issued for travel agencies, tour operators, hotels, and tourism-related services. Tourism licenses follow strict compliance rules due to consumer protection requirements.
  5. Freelancer / e-Trader License: Designed for individuals offering services or selling products online. These licenses support freelancers, influencers, and home-based digital businesses under regulated frameworks.

Each license has its own set of regulations and requirements. Must be vital to ensure that a company holds the appropriate one. It is based on its business activities.

What Information Can Be Verified from a Trade License

Once you access a trade license record, you can verify several important details.

License Number and Status

Confirms whether the license is active, expired, suspended, or cancelled.

Company / Trade Name & Owner Details

Shows the registered business name and, in many cases, ownership or shareholder information.

Business Activity / Permitted Operations

Lists approved activities, helping you confirm whether the company can legally provide specific services.

Issue & Expiry Dates

Helps you check license validity and renewal timelines.

Business Location (Mainland vs Free Zone)

Indicates whether the company operates under mainland authorities or a specific free zone.

Jurisdiction & Licensing Authority

Identifies the issuing authority, such as DED or a free zone authority, which matters for compliance and dispute handling.

How to Verify a Trade License in the UAE (Step-by-Step)

1. Step-by-Step Verification via DED Portal (Mainland Companies)

  1. Visit the official DED eServices portal
  2. Enter the license number or trade name
  3. Complete the CAPTCHA and search
  4. Open the full company profile
  5. Review license status and approved activities

This method works for all mainland companies registered in Dubai.

2. Verification via National Economic Register (NER)

  1. Visit the NER website: ner.economy.ae
  2. Enter the company name/license number. Type into the search bar.
  3. Review the company’s license information. These include its registered activities and license status, along with other pertinent details.

The NER is a useful tool. It confirms the legitimacy of any business in the UAE. This guarantees that the company is duly registered while complying with local regulations.

3. Verification for Free Zone Companies

Free zone companies use separate portals depending on jurisdiction:

  • DMCC
  • JAFZA
  • DAFZA
  • Dubai Internet City

Each free zone maintains its own verification system. Therefore, always check through the correct authority.

How to Interpret the Verification Results:

Here’s how you can interpret the verification results.

What “Active” License Means:

The business operates legally and meets renewal and compliance requirements.

What “Expired” License Means:

The license needs renewal. Proceed with caution and request an updated copy.

What “Suspended / Cancelled” License Means:

The company cannot legally operate. Avoid transactions immediately.

When Information Does Not Match (Possible Red Flag):

Mismatched names, activities, or addresses often signal inaccurate or fraudulent documentation.

How to Spot Fake or Invalid Trade Licenses

The following ways help you spot fake or invalid trade licenses. 

Mismatched License Number or Trade Name → Official portals should match the document exactly.

Wrong Expiry Dates or Missing Stamps → Valid licenses always show accurate dates and authority seals.

Outdated or Fake Logos on Documents → Authorities update branding regularly; outdated logos often indicate fake copies.

Unverifiable Business Address → If the address does not appear in official records, treat it as a warning sign.

Requests for Payment Without Documentation → Legitimate businesses provide invoices, contracts, and license copies upfront.

  2. Enter the company name/license number. Type into the search bar.
  3. Review the company’s license information. These include its registered activities and license status. Along with other pertinent details.

The NER is a useful tool. It confirms the legitimacy of any business in the UAE. This guarantees that the company is duly registered while complying with local regulations.

Emirate-Specific Department of Economic Development (DED) Portals

Each UAE emirate has its own Department of Economic Development portal. The respective DED allows users to verify trade licenses to their region. These portals provide accurate and up-to-date information. Particularly for businesses based in each emirate.

To UAE trade license check for businesses in the Emirates, below is the method:

  • Dubai: Visit the Dubai DED eServices Portal at eservices.dubaided.gov.ae. You can search for business information. Do so by entering the company’s name or license number.
  • Abu Dhabi: Go to the Abu Dhabi DED official website at added.gov.ae. Then, use the business license search feature. This way, you can check company details.
  • Sharjah: Access the Sharjah DED Online Portal at sedd.ae. Now, use the trade name search function to verify company information.
  • Other Emirates: Individuals must visit respective DED portals for license verification. Businesses based in Ajman, Fujairah, Ras Al Khaimah, and Umm Al Quwain have to visit:
    • Ajman: Ajman DED
    • Fujairah: Fujairah DED
    • Ras Al Khaimah: RAK DED
    • Umm Al Quwain: UAQ DED

These portals are an essential resource. Any business or individual leverages them for verifying trade licenses. In turn, they get assurance that their businesses comply with local regulations.

Alternative Methods for Trade License Verification

Online platforms offer the most convenient method for trade license verification. Still, there are alternative methods. Ideal for those who prefer direct communication or require additional confirmation.

1. Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation (MOHRE) Inquiry Services

The Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation provides an Inquiry Services portal. MOHRE portals allow users to access detailed information. They can have acknowledgment about UAE registered companies. This service is useful for verifying a company’s legal standing. Specifically in terms of labor laws and employment regulations.

Steps to verify a trade license using MOHRE:

  1. Visit the MOHRE Inquiry Services portal.
  2. Choose the “Company Information” service.
  3. Enter the company’s unique number or name. This way retrieves its license information.

This service is valuable to make sure that a business is legally licensed. It also assures that it is compliant with labor regulations.

2. Contacting DED Offices Directly

Contact the DED offices in the relevant emirate for more personalized service. DED is responsible for regulating businesses. They have the authority in issuing trade licenses in their jurisdiction. Reach out to the DED through phone inquiries or in-person visits.

How to contact the DED:

  1. Call the DED office of the relevant emirate or visit their website for contact details.
  2. Provide the company name or license number.
  3. Request verification of the company’s trade license status and any additional information.

Directly contacting the DED office allows for official confirmation and can be useful in cases where online information is inconclusive or outdated.

Tips for Accurate Trade License Verification

Follow a few best practices to achieve accuracy and reliability when verifying a trade license:

 

  1. Double-check the company name and license number: On entering the company name/license number, accuracy is critical. Minor spelling errors can prevent you from retrieving the correct information.
  2. Use official government websites: Always rely on official government portals. These are the DED websites and the NER. They have the most accurate and up-to-date information. You should avoid third-party websites. Because their data may be outdated or incorrect.
  3. Verify the license’s validity: Check that the trade license is active. It should not be expired. It must cover the company’s business activities. Verify the listed activities must align with what the company claims to be doing.
  4. Consult with professionals if needed: Consider seeking assistance if you’re unsure or facing difficulties during the verification process. Take it from business consultants or legal advisors. Those who specialize in UAE trade regulations.

What to Do If You Can’t Verify or the License Is Invalid

You have many options to do if you can’t verify the license or if it is invalid.

Stop Business Dealings Immediately:

Pause payments, contracts, and commitments until clarification.

Request Clarification or Updated License Copy:

Sometimes delays occur due to renewal processes.

Report to DED or Free Zone Authority:

Authorities actively investigate suspected violations.

Seek Legal or Professional Advice:

Consult business setup experts or legal advisors for next steps.

Common Issues and How to Troubleshoot

UAE trade license verification is straight. Some common issues that users may encounter. Here’s how to address them:

  1. License Not Found Online: Double-check the entered details. It could involve the company name or license number for accuracy. Still, if the issue persists, the license may have expired, or been suspended. It even means that the company may have changed its registration details.
  2. Outdated Information: Contact the DED if the company’s license information is outdated or incorrect. This way, you can report the discrepancy. The company should update its information with the authorities.
  3. Suspected Fraudulent Licenses: If you suspect a company is operating under a fraudulent license, gather all relevant information and report it to the DED or other relevant authorities.

Benefits of Regularly Verifying Trade Licenses

Enjoy many benefits of regularly verifying trade licenses:

Prevents Fraud & Financial Risks

Early checks save money and protect assets.

Ensures Regulatory Compliance

Verification supports compliance with UAE commercial laws.

Builds Trust in Partnerships

Transparency strengthens long-term business relationships.

Protects Business Reputation

Working only with licensed entities enhances credibility and brand value.

Conclusion

Trade license verification is an essential step. UAE Businesses having this document are assured that they are operating legally and ethically. Businesses and individuals can confirm the company’s legitimacy before entering into any transactions. They do so by leveraging the available online platforms and resources. It could be the National Economic Register and the Department of Economic Development portals. With advanced digital platforms and clear regulatory frameworks in 2025 and 2026, there’s no reason to skip this step.

This verification process helps to foster trust. Specifically in the UAE’s business environment. Ultimately, protects stakeholders from potential fraud and legal complications.

FAQs

Can I verify a trade license for free?

Yes, UAE authorities provide free online portals for mainland and free zone trade license verification.

Do free zone licenses show the same details as mainland licenses?

They show similar core details, but free zones may limit ownership or financial disclosures.

How to verify a UAE trade license online?

You can verify the UAE trade license online by using the relevant emirate’s economic department portal. This way, you can check the license status and validity.

How do I check if my company is active or not?

You can check whether your company is active or not by looking up the company name or license number on the government registry of the licensing authority.

What is a trade license in the UAE, and why is verification important?

A trade license legally permits you to perform a business activity. The verification process ensures that you’re working with a legitimate company.

What are the different types of trade licenses issued in the UAE?

The main types of trade licenses issued in the UAE include:

  • Commercial
  • Professional
  • Industrial
  • Tourism, and
  • Freelancer/e-Trader licenses.

What should I do if a trade license is not showing or appears expired during verification?

If it happens, you can ask the company for a recent license copy or check secondary registries. You can also request an extract from the licensing authority.

Are there alternative methods to verify a trade license besides online portals?

There are alternative methods also available to verify a trade license. You can request a physical license copy, extract from DED, or ask their PRO or government agent.
